name: Cambodia

nso.name: National Institute of Statistics (NIS), Ministry of Planning

latest_census.notes: General Population Census of Cambodia 2019 (3-12 March 2019; final results October 2020, with UNFPA support). Both the 2008 and 2019 censuses asked religion and mother tongue; neither asked ethnicity, and NIS reports ethnic minorities through mother tongue as the proxy. High confidence for 2008 (Buddhist ~97%, Khmer mother tongue ~95%); high that 2019 kept both items. 'Ethnicity not asked' is medium-high confidence - the questionnaire is a one-page check before declaring.

subnational_sources.title: General Population Census of Cambodia 2019 - National Report on Final Census Results (population by religion and by mother tongue, by province)
subnational_sources.matches_boundary_level: admin1 (25 provinces incl. Phnom Penh) exactly
subnational_sources.evidence: The 2019 national report follows the 2008 report's chapter structure, which had province-level religion and mother-tongue tables; hosted on nis.gov.kh.

subnational_sources.title: GPCC 2019 - Provincial Reports (one per province), with district-level tables
subnational_sources.matches_boundary_level: admin2 (197 shapes; Cambodia had roughly 200 districts in 2019, so near) if religion/mother tongue are tabulated by district
subnational_sources.evidence: NIS issued provincial volumes for 2008 with district tables; the 2019 round is expected to mirror that, but I cannot confirm that religion and mother tongue appear by district.

subnational_sources.title: CamStat - NIS statistical database (.Stat Suite instance) with census 2019 tables
subnational_sources.evidence: NIS launched a .Stat-based dissemination platform (camstat, on a nis.gov.kh subdomain) around 2020; whether census religion/mother-tongue tables are loaded there is unverified. If they are, this is the machine-readable route.

subnational_sources.title: General Population Census of Cambodia 2008 - National Report and Provincial Reports (religion, mother tongue by province and district)
subnational_sources.matches_boundary_level: admin1 near (24 vs 25: Tbong Khmum split from Kampong Cham in 2013)
subnational_sources.evidence: Fallback; boundaries predate the 2013 Tbong Khmum split named in the packet's admin1 sample.

subnational_sources.title: IPUMS-International - Cambodia 1998, 2008 (and possibly 2019) census samples
subnational_sources.evidence: Religion and mother tongue variables are in the Cambodian samples; registration required.

tier_reason: Census counts of religion and mother tongue exist by province (25 = admin1) in the 2019 national report, but the only format I can vouch for is PDF; CamStat may offer a table-builder/API but is unverified, and district-level tables are uncertain. Ethnicity is not a census item (mother tongue is the proxy).
recommended_action: Crawl nis.gov.kh for the 2019 final-results national report and read its religion and mother-tongue province tables with probe_pdf.py (25 provinces join by name - 'Siem Reap', 'Tbong Khmum'). Probe the CamStat instance for the same tables via its SDMX/.Stat API before settling for PDF. For the 197 districts, check the 2019 provincial reports. Declare ethnicity not_collected with the reason 'the census asks mother tongue, not ethnic group' after confirming on the 2019 questionnaire.
not_found: exact titles and URLs of the 2019 report PDFs and the CamStat instance
whether religion/mother tongue are tabulated by district in the 2019 provincial reports
an XLSX/CSV release of the 2019 census tables
summary: Cambodia's NIS (nis.gov.kh) counted religion and mother tongue in the 2019 census and publishes both by the 25 provinces (= admin1) in the final-results report (PDF), with district tables possible in the provincial volumes and a .Stat-based CamStat database that may expose the same machine-readably. Ethnicity is not asked; mother tongue is the office's proxy for ethnic minorities. Tier B pending a check of CamStat.
